situation:
You are to assume the role of operations manager at FIELD & FURROW BOWLS, a salad and grain bowl counter with three downtown locations. The founder (judge) has asked to meet with you about an offer that would change how every order leaves the counter.

FIELD & FURROW BOWLS opened two years ago on a single idea: every bowl, lid and fork handed across the counter is compostable, a pledge printed on the packaging and repeated in the company's email newsletter. The compostable bowl and lid cost sixty-two cents per order. The company's first round of funding runs out in about five months.

GREENLINE MARKETS, a regional grocery chain, has offered to stock four hundred FIELD & FURROW BOWLS salads a day in its stores. Its shelves require a sealed plastic bowl, which costs twenty-four cents per order, and the compostable bowl cannot be sealed. The account would carry the company well past the point where its funding runs out.

Accepting the GREENLINE MARKETS account would break the compostable pledge printed on the packaging and would disappoint the regular guests who chose the counter for it. Turning the account down would keep that pledge, at the cost of the revenue the company needs before its funding runs out, and would likely mean closing a location and the jobs in it.

The founder (judge) wants your recommendation, the written message the company would send to guests who ask about a change, and the directions counter staff should be given for answering the same question in person. The founder (judge) will begin the role-play by greeting you and asking to hear your ideas. After you have presented and have answered the founder's (judge's) questions, the founder (judge) will thank you for your work.
judgeCharacterization:
You are to assume the role of founder of FIELD & FURROW BOWLS, a salad and grain bowl counter with three downtown locations. Business background is the same as the situation above.

You have asked the operations manager (participant) to recommend whether to accept the GREENLINE MARKETS account, to draft the written message guests would receive, and to give the counter staff directions for answering the same question face to face.

During the course of the role-play you are to ask the participant the following questions:
judgeQuestions: A year from now, how will we know this was the right call?
What would tell us early that we chose wrong?
